characterization_methods.key_findings: Metallic character (nonzero DOS at the Fermi level); magnetic character from asymmetric spin up/down channels; for MnAl the -5 to 1 eV band range is determined mainly by Al-p and Mn-d bands; TDOS near the Fermi level is mainly low Al-p states hybridized with Mn-d states; Fermi surface mainly from Mn-d states with low Al-p contribution; no Fe-d contribution (Figure 3 panel j).
characterization_methods.purpose: Analyze chemical bonding and electronic structure of MnAl

characterization_methods.key_findings: Mn–Al-(110) total electron density contour map (Slice 1 scale 0.10–0.50) and electron density difference map (Slice 1 scale −0.05 to 0.05) indicate covalent and metallic bonding between Mn and Al.
characterization_methods.purpose: Analyze chemical bonding (covalent vs metallic) in MnAl
characterization_methods.technique: DFT electron density distribution maps (total and difference)

characterization_methods.key_findings: Mechanically stable (satisfies cubic stability criteria); C11=203.8, C12=152.9, C44=126.6 GPa; B=169.8, G=67.5, E=178.8 GPa; σ=0.324; H_V=5.0 GPa; B/G=2.52 (ductile); A^U=3.80, A_B=0, A_G=0.276, A1=A2=A3=4.97 (largest anisotropy among Fe-Mn-Al alloys).
characterization_methods.purpose: Assess mechanical stability, elastic moduli and mechanical anisotropy of MnAl
characterization_methods.technique: DFT elastic constants + Voigt-Reuss-Hill (VRH) approximation; elastic anisotropy indices

analytical_models.equation_role: Derive polycrystalline bulk modulus B, shear modulus G, Young's modulus E and Poisson's ratio σ from single-crystal elastic constants
Estimate Vickers hardness H_V from shear modulus G and bulk modulus B
analytical_models.model_note: H_V = 2(k²G)^0.585 − 3, k = G/B (Eq. 10); for MnAl H_V = 5.0 GPa.

analytical_models.equation_role: Calculate Debye temperature ΘD and longitudinal/transverse/average sound velocities (v_l, v_s, v_m) from B, G and ρ
analytical_models.model_name: Debye temperature and sound velocity model

analytical_models.equation_role: Calculate universal anisotropic index A^U, anisotropy A_B and A_G, and shear anisotropic factors A_1 = A_2 = A_3

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: 8×8×8 Monkhorst-Pack k-point mesh; maximum plane-wave cutoff energy 450 eV; total energy converged to 2×10⁻⁶ eV; force on each atom reduced to 0.5 eV/nm
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Ultrasoft pseudopotentials; GGA-PBE exchange-correlation; valence electron states Fe 3d⁶4s², Mn 3d⁵4s², Al 3s²3p¹
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated lattice parameters show good agreement with other experimental and calculated values (slight deviation attributed to differences in calculation methods and experimental conditions).

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Computational study with no experimental thermal/mechanical processing. Geometry-optimized crystal structure via first-principles DFT using CASTEP; GGA-PBE exchange-correlation, ultrasoft pseudopotentials, 8×8×8 Monkhorst-Pack k-point mesh, 450 eV plane-wave cutoff, energy converged to 2×10⁻⁶ eV and forces below 0.5 eV/nm.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: DFT (CASTEP, GGA-PBE) single-crystal elastic constants; polycrystalline B, G, E, σ derived by Voigt-Reuss-Hill (VRH) approximation.

electrical_properties.conductivity: metallic (nonzero DOS at the Fermi level); good electronic conductivity

magnetic_properties.magnetic_character: magnetic characteristics due to dissymmetric spin up/down DOS channels

phases_present.crystal_structure: cubic, space group Pm-3m (B2); a = b = c = 0.584 nm

structures.overall_structure: B2-type cubic Mn-Al compound (space group Pm-3m); cubic supercell (16-atom cell) with 8 Mn atoms on one simple-cubic sublattice and 8 Al atoms on the other (Fe-free end member, x = 1).

unmapped_findings: Lattice parameter of MnAl: a = b = c = 0.584 nm (Table 1). (source: b0021, b0019)
Cohesive energy E_coh = -6.568 eV·atom⁻¹ and formation enthalpy ΔH_f = -0.215 eV·atom⁻¹ (Table 1); both negative, indicating thermodynamic stability. (source: b0021, b0019, b0022)
Elastic constants (GPa): C11 = 203.8, C12 = 152.9, C44 = 126.6; MnAl has the smallest C44 (126.6 GPa) among the Fe1-xMnxAl alloys. (source: b0049, b0044)

Elastic moduli (VRH): bulk modulus B = 169.8 GPa, shear modulus G = 67.5 GPa, Young's modulus E = 178.8 GPa, Poisson's ratio σ = 0.324, B/G = 2.52; B/G > 1.75 indicates ductility. (source: b0049, b0044, b0045)

Anisotropy indices (dimensionless): A^U = 3.80, A_B = 0, A_G = 0.276, A_1 = A_2 = A_3 = 4.97; MnAl has the largest elastic anisotropy and the strongest shear-modulus anisotropy in (100), (010) and (001) planes among Fe-Mn-Al alloys. (source: b0051, b0059, b0063)

MnAl has the highest B/G ratio (2.52) and the lowest Debye temperature (504.1 K) in the series, indicating the strongest metallic character; it also has the lowest Vickers hardness (5.0 GPa). (source: b0075, b0047)
At the [100], [010], [001] and [110] directions, MnAl shows the minimum Young's modulus among the Fe1-xMnxAl alloys, reflecting strong directional dependence of Young's modulus. (source: b0064)
